A3:
**A3 — Increments a count (in the context of a loop)**

Award the point whenever the response increments some counter variable inside the body of a loop; that is the only thing this sub-item tests. Do not let the placement of the username assignment affect this decision. In particular, if the response assigns `username` (or `this.username`) once *after* the loop terminates rather than inside the loop, that is fully acceptable — the loop exits only when a candidate has passed `isAvailable`, so whatever name is stored is the one that passed the availability check, and the counter increment inside the loop still earns credit. Likewise, the response need not use the count as part of a candidate username and need not initialize the count; neither omission costs this point.

Deduct only when no count is incremented within a loop at all — for example, when the counter is increased only outside any loop, or when there is no increment of a counter anywhere in the response.
A4:
**A4 grading note.** Award the point only when the value stored in `username` is arrived at by consulting availability: there must be an `isAvailable` test that gates the assignment, and where the response builds a numbered candidate (`requestedName` + number), that candidate string must itself be (re)assigned inside the body of the loop so the loop is visibly trying new names.

Deduct if `username` is set directly from `requestedName` with no `isAvailable` call anywhere — i.e., availability is never consulted before the name is stored — since in that case the assignment is unconditional rather than gated by an availability test.

Do not deduct when the loop body recomputes the numbered candidate (e.g., reassigning `requestedName + count` each pass) before or as part of the availability check; this counts as a correct algorithm for this item even if the counter itself is never changed inside the loop, because the assigned string is not left stale and the loop is visibly attempting new candidate names.
